Petition under Section 166 and 140 of M.V. Act, 1988 for grant of compensation Award
1.

In the present claim petition, the petitioner Sh. Shatrughan is seeking compensation with respect to grievous injuries suffered by him in the accident which occurred on 17.12.2015 at 4:00 PM at NarelaAlipur Road, near Holambi Drain, Delhi, involving Car bearing registration no. DL3CT 0630(offending vehicle) being driven by respondent no. 1 Sh. Krishan Chand Saini in a rash and negligent manner.

2. Brief facts of the case are that as per Detailed Accident Report(DAR), on 17.12.2015 at about 4.00 PM, the petitioner was going towards Holambi on motorcycle bearing registration no. DL8SAG 6362 and when he reached at NarelaAlipur Road, near Holambi Drain, Delhi, the driver of the offending vehicle which was moving ahead of him slowed down the speed and suddenly opened the gate of driver's side of offending vehicle, as a result of which, his motorcycle hit against the door of offending vehicle and he alongwith motorcycle fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.

He was taken to the clinic of Dr. Mukesh Aggarwal by MACP No. 6771/16; FIR No. 409/16 ;
PS. Narela DOD: 15.02.2023 respondent no. 1 where he was medically examined.
Thereafter nothing happened for next five months and on 27.05.2016 the petitioner went to Police Station Narela and got his statement recorded.
It is stated that FIR No. 409/16, Under Section 279/337 IPC was registered at PS. Narela with regard to the said accident.
It is stated that offending vehicle was owned by respondent no. 1 himself and insured with respondent no.2 at the time of accident.

3. In his written statement, the respondent no. 1 i.e. drivercum owner raised preliminary objection that alleged accident had not been caused with offending vehicle and he has been falsely implicated in the present case.
It has been claimed that he was having valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
It has been further claimed that offending vehicle was insured with respondent no. 2 at the time of accident.
On merits, he has denied the averments made in DAR and prayed for its dismissal.

4. Respondent no.3/insurance company filed its reply stating therein that as per the statement of injured, the accident had taken place on 17.12.2015 and he was admitted in Dr. Mukesh Orthopedic & Trauma Centre by the respondent no. 1 but no MLC was prepared in the said hospital.
It has been claimed that neither the injured informed the police nor he disclosed to the doctor in the hospital about the accident.

It has also been claimed that accident took place on 17.12.2015 whereas FIR was MACP No. 6771/16; FIR No. 409/16 ; PS. Narela DOD: 15.02.2023 registered on 27.05.2016 i.e.
after about 5 months 10 days of the accident and the MLC of injured was prepared in SRHC Hospital on 27.05.2016.
It has been claimed that there are no medical documents to show that injured had suffered the injuries in a road accident.
It has also been claimed that the offending vehicle was falsely implicated by the injured in the present case in order to extort money.
On the basis of these averments, On the basis of these averments, it has denied the averments made in the DAR and prayed for its dismissal.

From the pleadings of the parties, the following issues were framed by my Ld. Predecessor vide order dated 29.04.2017:
1.

Whether the injured Shatrughan suffered injuries in road traffic accident on 17.12.2015 at 4.00 PM at Alipur Holambi Road, Near Minda Farm House, Delhi within the jurisdiction of PS. Narela due to rashness and negligence on the part of the Krishan Chand Saini who was driving Car bearing registration no. DL3CT0630, owned by Sh. Krishan Chand Saini and insured with IFFCO Tokio General Insurance Co. Ltd?OPP.
2.

sentences.text: Whether the injured is entitled to any compensation if so to what amount and from whom?OPP.

3. Relief.
6.
In support of his claim, the petitioner has examined two witnesses i.e. himself as PW1 and PW2 Dr. Ashutosh Gupta.

His evidence MACP No. 6771/16; FIR No. 409/16 ; PS. Narela DOD:
15.02.2023 was closed vide order dated 03.05.2019.
On the other hand, no evidence was adduced by any of the respondents and their respective evidence was closed vide order dated 20.09.2019.
7. Before proceeding further, it may be noted that vide order dated 29.11.19 passed by my Ld.

Predecessor, it was directed that the petitioner shall not be entitled to any interest from 29.11.2019 till further orders as he had failed to conclude his evidence despite grant of sufficient time and opportunities.
Record shows that PE was concluded on 04.09.2020.
Thus, his right to claim interest has been curtailed from 29.11.19 till 04.09.2020.
8. I have heard the arguments addressed by ld counsels for the parties.
I have also gone through the record.

My findings on the issues are as under:
9.

Since this is a claim petition under Section 166 and 140 of Motor Vehicles Act and to be held entitled for the compensation on account of injury suffered by him, the petitioner is required to prove the negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.

The petitioner is seeking compensation with regard to the grievous injuries suffered by him in the accident which occurred on 27.05.2016 at 4:00 PM at NarelaAlipur Road, near Holambi Drain, Delhi, involving Car bearing registration no. DL3CT MACP No. 6771/16; FIR No. 409/16 ; PS. Narela DOD: 15.02.2023 0630(offending vehicle) being driven by respondent no. 1 Sh. Krishan Chand Saini in a rash and negligent manner.
10. For the purposes of this issue, the testimony of petitioner/PW1 is relevant.
PW1 has deposed in his evidence by way of affidavit (Ex. PW1/A) on the lines of averments made in DAR.
He has relied upon the following documents: S.No.
Description of documents Remarks 1. His treatment record Ex PW1/1(colly)
2. Original medical bills
Ex. PW1/2(colly)

6. His disability certificate issued Ex. PW1/5 by SRHC Hospital 11.
During his crossexamination on behalf of insurance company, he deposed that he had told the concerned doctor of Mukesh Hospital that he had sustained injuries in a road traffic accident.
He further deposed that it is not within his knowledge if the said fact was mentioned by said doctor in his treatment record or not.
He deposed that the offending vehicle was going ahead at a distance of about 1520 meters from his motorcycle.

He MACP No. 6771/16; FIR No. 409/16 ; PS. Narela DOD:
15.02.2023 admitted that there was no road divider and it was a single road where the accident had taken place.
He further deposed that his motorcycle was at a distance of about 1520 meters when the driver of offending vehicle suddenly applied brakes.
He again said that the driver of the offending vehicle had not applied the sudden brakes but slowed down the speed of offending vehicle and suddenly opened the driver side door of the car.

He denied the suggestion that he had been driving his motorcycle at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner or that he could not control his motorcycle due to which, he hit his motorcycle against the door of the offending vehicle.
He denied the suggestion that he had not been wearing helmet at the time of accident or that the accident had taken place due to his sole negligence.
He further denied the suggestion that there was no negligence on the part of the driver of offending vehicle.

He denied the suggestion that he had not made any PCR call at 100 number on the day of accident or that he had not informed the concerned doctor that he had sustained any injuries due to road traffic accident or that is why the same had not been mentioned in his treatment record of Mukesh Hospital.
He deposed that he had visited the police station Narela after about 45 months from the date of accident.

He volunteered that driver Sh. Krishan Chander Saini had promised him to bear the entire medical expenses and had requested not to lodge any police complaint with regard to road accident and he had himself removed him to Mukesh Hospital and had also borne the medical expenses of about Rs. 11,888/
regarding his treatment received from Mukesh Hospital.

He denied the suggestion that he had not MACP No. 6771/16; FIR No. 409/16 ; PS. Narela DOD: 15.02.2023 immediately lodged police complaint after the accident because the accident had taken place due to his sole negligence.
12.

It is argued on behalf of insurance company that no FIR with regard to the present case was registered on the date of accident and even there was no DD entry recorded on the date of accident regarding the accident in question.
He further argued that accident had taken place on 17.12.2015 and FIR in the present case was lodged on 27.05.2016 i.e. after about 5 months 10 days of the accident.
He also argued that there are no medical documents to show that the petitioner had suffered the injuries as alleged by him in the road accident.
He vehemently argued that there is nothing on record that the petitioner had suffered injuries in road traffic accident.
He also argued that there is also nothing on record to show that the respondent no.1 was negligent while driving the alleged offending vehicle.
That without holding the negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle, the insurance company shall not be liable to pay compensation.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A perusal of the DAR filed in the matter makes a shocking revelation.

Firstly, there is no police report with regard to the accident lodged by the petitioner either on the date of accident i.e.
17.12.2015 or immediately thereafter.
Even FIR in the present case was lodged on 27.05.2016 on the statement of petitioner i.e. almost after five months of the accident.
Secondly, there is no document on record showing that the MACP No. 6771/16; FIR No. 409/16 ; PS. Narela DOD: 15.02.2023 petitioner had sustained injuries in the road traffic accident.

Even first medical treatment document i.e. prescription dated 17.12.2015 of Dr. Mukesh Aggarwal does not find mention anywhere that the petitioner was removed there with alleged history of RTA.
14.
It is apparent on record that the petitioner kept mum for almost 5 months after the accident and then got the FIR registered on 27.05.2016 with the police.
Rule 7 of Delhi Motor Accident Claim Tribunal Rules, 2008 carries presumption of genuineness of reports filed by the police which is reproduced as under: "7. Presumption about reports.

entities.text: Delhi Motor Accident Claim Tribunal Rules, 2008
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
The contents of reports submitted to the Claims Tribunal in Form "A" and Form "D" by investigating police officer and concerned registering authority respectively, and confirmation under clause (b) of rule 5 by the insurance company shall be presumed to be correct, and shall be read in evidence without formal proof, till proved to the contrary".
15.
The authenticity of the aforesaid police report can not be disputed, however the conduct of the petitioner is not above board.
It is evident that there is nothing on record which could show that the petitioner had sustained injuries in a road traffic accident.

It appears that as an afterthought to receive money from the insurance company as the offending vehicle was insured at the time of accident, the petitioner appeared to have filed the FIR in the matter without placing on record any document proving the fact that he had actually suffered injuries in the road traffic accident MACP No. 6771/16; FIR No. 409/16 ; PS. Narela DOD: 15.02.2023 caused by respondent no. 1 while driving the offending vehicle.
The conduct of the petitioner on the face of record is not bonafide.
The Motor Vehicle Act is a Welfare Legislation but that welfare can not be stretched to such a limit where an injured could be permitted to take the Tribunal for a ride for his vested gains.
The petitioner wants this Tribunal to consider his claim on equitable consideration.
It is settled norm that one who seeks equity from the court has to do equity himself.
Accordingly, the petitioner has not been able to prove its case while placing reliance upon the DAR in the present case.

There is no other material on record which shows that the petitioner had sustained injuries in a road traffic accident which was caused by respondent no. 1 while driving the offending vehicle in a rash and negligent manner.

16. Hence, in view of above discussion it is held that the petitioner has failed to prove even on the principles of preponderence of probabilities that he had suffered grievous injuries in the accident which occurred on 17.12.2015 at 4:00 PM at NarelaAlipur Road, near Holambi Drain, Delhi, due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no. 1.
Issue no.1 is accordingly decided in favour of respondents and against the petitioner.

5 17. In view of findings on issue no.1(supra), it is clear that the petitioner has failed to prove the negligence on the part of driver of MACP No. 6771/16; FIR No. 409/16 ; PS. Narela DOD:
15.02.2023 offending vehicle.

Since, this is a claim petition under Section 166 and 140 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and the petitioner has failed to prove the negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle, on the basis of preponderence of probabilities, hence he is not entitled to any compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act.
18. In view of findings on issues no.1 and 2 (supra), present claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is dismissed.
File be consigned to record room after due compliance.
